title: How far does the Earth travel around the Sun in a week?
description: The Earth travels about nine hundred forty million kilometres around the Sun in a year. The video matches a year with fifty two weeks, and divides the distance by that same number to find one week.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the time is divided by a number, the distance is divided by the same number. Watch for students who divide the yearly distance by seven, which is the days in a week and not the weeks in a year.

source: Figure it Out (rule of three, question 1)
video_script.why: A year is about fifty two weeks, so the same factor of change that scaled the rice scales the distance.
video_script.substitution: Write weeks to distance for a year and for one week, then divide the yearly distance by fifty two.
video_script.anchor: the Earth going once around the Sun in a year, from the book
video_script.payoff_line: The Earth travels about eighteen million seventy six thousand nine hundred twenty three kilometres in a week

final_answer.spoken: about eighteen million seventy six thousand nine hundred twenty three kilometres in a week

never_show: 940000000 ÷ 7 as the distance in a week, marked as right
maths_rules: one year is taken as about 52 weeks
check: 18 million × 52 = 936 million, close to 940 million; 18076923 × 52 = 939999996
video_script.design: One idea: match a year with fifty two weeks, then divide the distance by the same number. The Earth and Sun picture stays on the stage and the proportion sits on the board.
